title: Board liaison QBR brief + customer recap email (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working draft intended for CSMs who need a concise, board-liaison-style QBR brief and a pair of customer-facing quarterly recap email templates. Use this when your executive sponsor is senior (VP+/board liaison) and wants a short, high-signal summary plus an optional client-facing recap to land after the meeting.

How to use this doc:
- Fill placeholders ({{customer_name}}, {{quarter}}, {{sponsor_name}}, {{renewal_date}}) before sending.
- Keep the board-liaison brief to one side page (under 400 words).
- Attach an appendix with the metrics snapshot if the sponsor asks for detail.

Deliverables in this file:
1) One-page board-liaison QBR brief (talking points + risk heatmap).
2) Two customer-facing quarterly recap email variants (short exec note + detailed operational recap).
3) A compact renewal readiness checklist and quick tracker snippet for the CSM.

1) One-page board-liaison QBR brief (single-slide / email body)
- Header: {{customer_name}} — QBR ({{quarter}}) — Sponsor briefing (for {{sponsor_name}})
- TL;DR (1 sentence): "Usage steady; material ROI realized; recommended: continue current deployment + approve one pilot of Feature X to reduce latency and cost."
- Top 3 wins since last QBR:
  1. Delivery: Average inference latency down from 260ms -> 180ms after routing changes; peak p95 improved by 28%.
  2. Cost: Unit token cost reduced 12% through quantization and batching recommendations.
  3. Product: Integration of dedicated model variant eliminated 2x timeout incidents.
- Key risk(s) (one line each) and mitigation:
  - Renewability timing: contract up {{renewal_date}} — risk: procurement cycle lengthening by 4–6 weeks. Mitigation: prep pre-approved T&Cs + finance PO template.
  - Data residency ask: small percentage of requests require on-prem keying — Mitigation: PVN/private deployment options scoped; exec commit needed.
- One metric snapshot (single-line bullets):
  - MRR impact this quarter: +${{delta_mrr}} (expansion: ${{expansion}}; churn: ${{churn}})
  - Avg daily QPS: {{qps}}; Average latency: {{avg_latency}}ms; Model accuracy proxy (NPS / eval pass rate): {{eval_pass_rate}}%
- Ask / decision needed from sponsor (explicit):
  1) Approve pilot budget ${{pilot_budget}} for Feature X (3 months).
  2) Align procurement lead to target renewal on or before {{renewal_target_date}}.
- Suggested next steps (for the sponsor):
  - 15-min sync to sign off on pilot scope (owner: CSM).
  - Introduce procurement to finance contact (owner: Customer Success Manager).

2) Customer-facing quarterly recap emails (two variants)
A. Short executive recap (one-paragraph, for C-level sponsor)
Subject line suggestions:
  - "Quarterly update — {{customer_name}} & Redwood Inference ({{quarter}})"
  - "{{customer_name}} QBR highlights (quick)"
Email body (short):
  Hi {{sponsor_name}},

  Thank you for partnering with us this quarter. Quick highlights: latency improved ~30% after routing optimizations, we reduced token unit cost ~12% through batching/quantization, and your team saw a 2.1% lift in customer-facing feature conversion where the model is embedded. We recommend a short pilot of Feature X to accelerate the next phase of cost and latency improvements — estimated pilot budget ${{pilot_budget}} for 3 months.

  Would you be open to a 15-minute alignment call next week to confirm scope and procurement owners?

  Best,
  {{csm_name}} — Redwood Inference

B. Detailed operational recap (longer, includes attachments/appendix)
Subject line suggestions:
  - "{{customer_name}} QBR: performance, usage, and roadmap items ({{quarter}})"
Email body (detailed):
  Hi {{sponsor_name}} and team,

  Thanks for the time on the QBR earlier. Below is a concise record of what we covered and the next steps. I attached a short appendix with the raw metrics and a renewal readiness snapshot.

  1) Summary of results:
    - Latency: p95 improved from 260ms -> 180ms after routing and cache tweaks; peak-hour throughput increased by 35%.
    - Cost: per-token compute spend reduced by 12% vs prior quarter (mix of batching + mixed-precision quant).
    - Reliability: Incidents reduced from 4->1 (root cause: network flapping; mitigated via region failover).

  2) Usage & ROI highlights:
    - Average monthly active requests: {{mau_requests}}
    - Measured conversion lift on product flow Y: +2.1% correlating to ~$ {{estimated_revenue_uplift}} in incremental ARR.

  3) Roadmap asks & pilot suggestion:
    - Pilot Feature X (3-month): estimated pilot budget ${{pilot_budget}}; expected latency saving ~15–25% on targeted flows.
    - Data residency exploration: we scoped private deployment; next step: 30-min technical assessment with infra lead.

  4) Renewal readiness & timeline:
    - Current contract end: {{renewal_date}}.
    - Recommended internal milestones: procurement kick 8 weeks before renewal, legal review 6 weeks before.
    - CSM action: provide PO template and pricing terms on request.

  5) Open risks and blockers:
    - Delayed procurement leads to feature launch slippage.
    - Customer security team needs HSM/KMS detail — action: SRE to provide architecture note.

  Next steps (owners & dates):
    - CSM: Send PO template and appendix (by {{csms_send_date}}).
    - Product: Prepare pilot spec and success metrics (by {{product_spec_date}}).
    - Customer: Confirm procurement contact and timeline (by {{customer_commit_date}}).

  Attachments: performance-appendix-{{quarter}}.pdf; renewal-readiness-sheet-{{customer_name}}.xlsx

  Thanks again — happy to walk through any section.

  Cheers,
  {{csm_name}} (Customer Success Manager)

3) Renewal readiness quick checklist (one-paragraph checklist for CSM)
- Contract: Check existing term/end date and auto-renew flags.
- Procurement: Confirm PO process, payment terms, lead contact and typical cycle length.
- Executive alignment: Has sponsor indicated budget window? Follow-up within 6–8 weeks.
- Technical blockers: Open security/arch tickets; any unresolved incident that impacts SLA?
- Value metrics: Ensure delta MRR and measured ROI are documented and attached to the renewal packet.

Compact renewal tracker (copy into your tracking sheet)
- Customer: {{customer_name}}
- Renewal date: {{renewal_date}}
- Sponsor: {{sponsor_name}} (email: {{sponsor_email}})
- CSM: {{csm_name}}
- Current ARR: ${{current_arr}}
- Expansion pipeline: ${{expansion_pipeline}}
- Risk level: LOW | MED | HIGH (select)
- Next internal checkpoint: {{next_checkpoint_date}}

Communication cadence recommendations: first week post-QBR send the short exec recap; within 3 business days send the detailed recap to product and ops leads; schedule renewal alignment 8–10 weeks before renewal date.

Tone guide (short): keep exec notes high signal, <6 bullets, no deep technical language. For the operational recap use metrics and attach raw exports.

Sample elevator talking points for sponsor call (bullet list):
- "In three bullets: what improved, what it saved, what we need you to approve."
- "We saw a measurable conversion lift tied to our model changes — pilot will increase that uplift or lock savings."
- "If procurement can target signoff by {{renewal_target_date}}, we avoid a 6–8 week procurement slip and keep roadmap momentum."

Version history / notes:
- v0.1 (2025-11-15) initial draft (Aisha).
- v0.2 (2026-01-08) added pilot financial framing (Marco).
- v0.3 (2026-03-09) editorial pass and added sample subject lines + attachments list (Sofia).

Open questions (for CSM to resolve before finalizing):
- Confirm exact delta MRR and attach proof-of-value artifacts.
- Verify sponsor preferred cadence & email address.
- Confirm whether legal requires a redlined amendment for pilot budget.

Checklist before send:
- Replace all {{placeholders}}.
- Attach metrics appendix and renewal-readiness spreadsheet.
- Run subject line A/B on internal test thread for clarity.

End of document.
